lesson.text: Quick memory: what kind of line looks like calm water? (A wavy line.) Today: mixing colours with paint.
In painting, the three primary colours are red, yellow and blue. They are the starting colours: mix them in pairs and you get many more.
Mix two primary colours to make a secondary colour. Red and yellow make orange.
Yellow and blue make green, and blue and red make purple. Orange, green and purple are the secondary colours.
A tint is a colour mixed with white: it becomes lighter. Red and white make pink. Add the white a little at a time.
A shade is a colour mixed with black: it becomes darker. Blue and black make dark blue. Black is strong, so add only a tiny bit.
Mix all three primary colours together and you get a muddy brown. Wash your brush in water between colours to keep them bright.
Try it in the world: look at the flowers and blocks in your world. Which are primary colours, and which are secondary? Can you find a light tint and a dark shade?

exercises.prompt: Which are the three primary colours in paint?
exercises.hint: They are the three starting colours on the colour wheel.
exercises.explain: Red, yellow and blue are the primary colours in paint.

exercises.prompt: What colour do red and yellow make?
exercises.hint: Picture the two paints swirling together. Which colour sits between them on the colour wheel?
exercises.explain: Red and yellow make orange.

exercises.prompt: What colour do yellow and blue make?
exercises.hint: Picture the two paints swirling together. Which colour sits between them on the colour wheel?
exercises.explain: Yellow and blue make green.

exercises.prompt: What colour do blue and red make?
exercises.hint: Picture the two paints swirling together. Which colour sits between them on the colour wheel?
exercises.explain: Blue and red make purple.

exercises.prompt: Orange, green and purple are secondary colours.
exercises.hint: Is each one made by mixing two primaries?
exercises.explain: True: each is two primary colours mixed together.

exercises.prompt: Match each pair of paints to the colour it makes.
exercises.hint: Picture each pair swirling together.
exercises.explain: Red and yellow make orange, yellow and blue make green, blue and red make purple.

exercises.prompt: Which two primary colours make green?
exercises.hint: On a colour wheel, green sits between the two that make it.
exercises.explain: Yellow and blue make green.

exercises.prompt: What is a tint?
exercises.hint: A tint is lighter than the colour you started with.
choices: a colour mixed with water only
exercises.explain: A tint is a colour mixed with white, so it is lighter.

exercises.prompt: What do you make when you mix red and white?
exercises.hint: White makes a colour lighter.
exercises.explain: Red and white make pink, a tint of red.

exercises.prompt: Adding black to a colour makes a shade.
exercises.hint: Does black make a colour lighter or darker?
exercises.explain: True: a colour mixed with black is a shade, and it is darker.

exercises.prompt: Sort these colours: primary or secondary?
exercises.hint: Is it one of the three starting colours, or mixed from two of them?
exercises.explain: Primary: red, blue, yellow. Secondary (mixed from two primaries): orange, green, purple.

exercises.prompt: Zara mixed blue with black, and now it is far too dark. What should she have done?
exercises.hint: Black is very strong.
choices: added only a tiny bit of black
exercises.explain: Black is strong: add only a tiny bit at a time, and check as you go.

exercises.prompt: What do you add to purple to make lilac, a light purple?
exercises.hint: Is lilac lighter or darker than purple?
exercises.explain: Lilac is lighter than purple, so you add white: it is a tint of purple.

exercises.prompt: Mix orange in the bowl: tap the paint pots to add drops.
exercises.hint: Picture the two paints swirling together. Which colour sits between them on the colour wheel?
exercises.explain: Orange: red and yellow, the same number of drops of each.

exercises.prompt: Mix green in the bowl.
exercises.hint: Picture the two paints swirling together. Which colour sits between them on the colour wheel?
exercises.explain: Green: yellow and blue, the same number of drops of each.

exercises.prompt: Mix purple in the bowl.
exercises.hint: Picture the two paints swirling together. Which colour sits between them on the colour wheel?
exercises.explain: Purple: red and blue, the same number of drops of each.

exercises.prompt: Make pink, a tint of red, in the bowl.
exercises.hint: A tint is a colour with white mixed in.
exercises.explain: Pink: red and white, the same number of drops of each.

exercises.prompt: Make dark blue, a shade of blue, in the bowl.
exercises.hint: A shade is a colour with black mixed in.
exercises.explain: Dark blue: blue and black, the same number of drops of each.

exercises.prompt: Make brown in the bowl.
exercises.hint: Which colour do you get when you mix every primary colour?
exercises.explain: Brown: red, yellow and blue, all three primary colours together.

exercises.prompt: Make light green, a tint of green, in the bowl.
exercises.hint: First: which two primaries make green? Then: what makes a colour lighter?
exercises.explain: Light green: yellow and blue make green, and white makes it lighter.

exercises.prompt: Make lilac, a light purple, in the bowl.
exercises.hint: First: which two primaries make purple? Then: what makes a colour lighter?
exercises.explain: Lilac: red and blue make purple, and white makes it lighter.

exercises.prompt: Put these reds in order, from the lightest to the darkest.
exercises.hint: A tint has white in it; a shade has black in it.
exercises.explain: Pink (red with white, a tint), then red, then dark red (red with black, a shade).

exercises.prompt: What do you get if you mix all three primary colours together?
exercises.hint: Each colour you add makes the paint darker and muddier.
exercises.explain: All three primary colours make a muddy brown.

exercises.prompt: Bram's green looks too blue. What should he add?
exercises.hint: Green is made from two colours. Which one does it need more of?
exercises.explain: Green is yellow and blue. Adding more yellow makes it less blue and more yellowy.

exercises.prompt: A shade is lighter than the colour you started with.
exercises.hint: What does black do to a colour?
exercises.explain: False: a shade has black in it, so it is darker. A tint, with white, is lighter.
